items.note: Describes the central offset (prolongation of the central buttress) of the Śikhara of the Nilakaṇṭheśvara Temple, Udayapur, firm in contour against deep shadow.
Latā band carved on three levels with tiers (Bhūmis), lace pattern and Gavākṣa-net over the Śikhara face.
Śukanāsā images in the round from Kīrttimukha to Kīrttimukha; only the right-hand group is preserved.
Main Śukanāsā at Nilakaṇṭheśvara Temple, Udayapur: a blind with trefoil arch, shrine and images below, dancing Śiva and goddesses in the circle above.
Śukanāsā is a blind façade extended upward from the Antarāla (antechamber/porch of the Garbhagṛha).

Continues the Udayapur Śukanāsā description (Pls. XLVIII-XLIX): Antarāla as the link between Maṇḍapa and Prāsāda, with keel-vaulted superstructure and a five-storeyed mansion showing Śiva in many forms; chunk itself does not name the temple.
Side view of the Antarāla superstructure of the Nilakaṇṭheśvara Temple, Udayapur; profiles run round the building; five-storeyed mansion of the gods on pillars only.
South entrance balcony of the Maṇḍapa: steps over base mouldings, Vedi with dwarf railing and attendant goddesses in high relief; main entrance in East is of the same kind.
Interior of the Nilakaṇṭheśvara Temple, Udayapur: Nandin, pillars, carved doorway; two Antarāla pillars; the Ekamukha sheath of the Liṅga belongs to a later age.
Maṇḍapa pillar dimensions: square base 2'9", octagonal part 3'8" high, circular section 1'3"; square-octagon-circle transition described as the rule in mediaeval pillars.
